title: How to use CoRCA
keywords: start begin overview platform corca work workflow onboarding setup next ready started getting use usage next
body: CoRCA helps a team investigate microservice incidents. Connect monitoring in Settings → Connect & verify, discover and select services in Services & sensitivity, save their real dependencies, and set sensitivity. Then open Diagnoses, choose New diagnosis, and enter when the incident began. Review suspected services and unexplained symptoms against your monitoring and logs. Share the diagnosis link or download its JSON. CoRCA is a self-hosted beta for one trusted team, not an automatic remediation system.
summary:
1. Connect monitoring in Settings → Connect & verify.
2. Select services, save dependencies, and set sensitivity in Services & sensitivity.
3. Open Diagnoses and enter the incident start.
Review the findings against your dashboards and logs.

title: Connect your monitoring
keywords: connect connection adapter integration integrations provider prometheus grafana datadog dynatrace relic credentials endpoint token metrics monitoring otel opentelemetry collector
body: In Settings → Connect & verify, choose Prometheus, Grafana Cloud Metrics, Datadog, Dynatrace, or New Relic. Enter the endpoint and provider API credentials shown, then choose Verify & connect. Use read-only credentials. Choose your region where offered. Prometheus authentication is optional. Optional Metric settings define queries, labels, and resolution. Queries must return one series per service; aggregate duplicate series by the service label. Failed verification preserves the existing connection. Reconnecting replaces the source and clears sensitivity. An administrator manages connections. OpenTelemetry sends metrics through your Collector to a historical backend; CoRCA is not an OTLP receiver. There is no provider OAuth login.
summary: Open Settings → Connect & verify, choose your provider, and enter its endpoint and read-only API credentials. Choose Verify & connect, then discover services. An administrator manages connections. Optional Metric settings handle custom queries and labels.

title: Fix a connection problem
keywords: unavailable unauthorized forbidden expired rejected cannot failed fail failure connect connection credentials network hostname localhost docker endpoint empty series reachable verify
body: Check the provider region, endpoint, read permission, and query service label. The endpoint must be reachable from the CoRCA server/container. Inside Docker, localhost means the CoRCA container; host.docker.internal reaches a backend on the host. An administrator must allow private/custom hostnames through CORCA_ALLOWED_SOURCE_HOSTS on the deployment host. Use Verify metrics to check recent access; this is a timestamped check, not continuous connection monitoring. Never paste API keys or passwords into help chat. Ask an administrator to reconnect with fresh credentials when a provider rejects access.
summary: Check the provider region, endpoint, read permissions, and service label. Use Verify metrics to test recent access. In Docker, localhost means the CoRCA container; use host.docker.internal for a backend on your host. Ask an administrator to reconnect expired credentials.

title: Select services and dependencies
keywords: services scope topology graph dependencies dependency discover discovery caller callee missing coverage reporting
body: Open Services and choose Discover services to review observed metric coverage. An administrator selects services and saves caller → callee dependencies, or confirms that the selected services are independent. Discovery reads configured metric queries; it does not infer dependencies. Missing metrics or gaps can hide causes. Saved service scope remains visible during provider outages. Adding latency and error metrics extends coverage beyond CPU and memory. Changing scope or dependencies clears sensitivity/calibration and requires setting it again.
summary: Open Services and choose Discover services. An administrator selects the services and saves caller → callee dependencies, or confirms they are independent. Discovery shows metric coverage; it does not infer dependencies. Missing metrics can hide causes.

title: Set investigation sensitivity
keywords: sensitivity threshold thresholds calibration calibrated tau baro circa heuristic manual accuracy
body: After saving services and dependencies, an administrator sets an anomaly threshold in Services. The manual BARO starting value 6 is a heuristic, not environment calibration or an accuracy guarantee. A higher threshold usually returns fewer additional suspects. Saving manual sensitivity replaces loaded calibration and enables BARO. Advanced calibration must match the telemetry, service scope, topology, and current stopping/feature policies. CIRCA requires compatible calibration; it is not enabled just by setting a manual BARO threshold. Validate thresholds against independently confirmed incidents and healthy periods.
summary: After saving services and dependencies, an administrator sets sensitivity in Services. Manual BARO threshold 6 is a starting heuristic, not calibrated accuracy. A higher threshold usually returns fewer additional suspects. CIRCA needs compatible calibration.

title: Start and follow a diagnosis
keywords: diagnosis diagnoses incident investigation investigate root cause time window queue queued waiting data retry retries cancel running failed capacity completed analysis investigations investigate investigating started
body: In Diagnoses, choose New diagnosis and enter the incident start. CoRCA compares the healthy window before that time with the period after it. Default windows are 5 minutes before and 2 after, increased for coarse provider resolution; vendor minute-level metrics need at least 10 minutes on each side. Waiting for data means the incident window and scrape lag have not finished. Queued means waiting for capacity; Analyzing means metrics retrieval and ranking are in progress. Temporary request failures retry up to three attempts, 30 seconds apart. Cancel queued work if no longer needed. Running work cannot be cancelled in this beta. Failed jobs show an error; check the provider and source configuration. Setup must be completed before diagnoses can run.
summary: Open Diagnoses, choose New diagnosis, and enter the incident start. Waiting for data means CoRCA needs the rest of the time window; Queued means waiting for capacity. You can cancel queued work. For failures, check monitoring and source configuration.

title: Understand findings and uncertainty
keywords: result results findings evidence confidence score scores probability probabilities suspects partial weak unexplained insufficient healthy anomaly accuracy root cause why partly explained explanation explain
body: Suspected root causes are investigation leads, not independently confirmed incident causes. Score shares and anomaly-score ratios are not probabilities. Partly explained results retain unexplained symptoms. Missing or unusable metrics can hide causes; insufficient evidence does not mean the system is healthy. No significant anomaly means the available data did not cross the configured threshold, not a guarantee that nothing is wrong. Weak evidence should be checked against the incident start, service coverage, topology, and dashboards. Uploaded log findings are separate observations. CoRCA does not promise a production accuracy percentage.
summary: Partly explained means some significant symptoms remain unexplained. Treat suspected causes as investigation leads: scores are not probabilities. Check the incident start, missing metrics, and service dependencies against your dashboards. Insufficient evidence does not mean the system is healthy.

title: Connect and understand alerts
keywords: alert alerts alerting alertmanager webhook firing resolved receiver routing silence rule delivery automatic notification
body: Alerts opens on firing alerts. Search by alert or service; choose All alerts or Resolved to review history. Each receipt shows the latest reported state and a diagnosis link when a job exists. Connect alerts opens connection settings: enter a reachable CoRCA address, copy the receiver configuration into Alertmanager, and route chosen alerts to corca. Send a real firing alert to confirm delivery. Automatic diagnoses need monitoring, saved services/dependencies, and sensitivity. The page updates every five seconds while visible. Alert delivery confirmed means a real webhook was received in the past, not a continuously healthy sender. Rules, routes, and silences stay in Alertmanager. There is no direct email/SMS/pager notification service in CoRCA. Local receiver tests do not prove external delivery or queue a diagnosis. With individual accounts, the separate service token is required for webhook delivery.
summary: Open Alerts to see firing alerts and diagnosis links. Choose All alerts or Resolved for history. To connect, open Connection settings, copy the receiver into Alertmanager, and route alerts to corca. A real firing alert confirms delivery; a local test checks CoRCA only. Rules and silences stay in Alertmanager.

title: Upload and analyze logs
keywords: log logs file files upload uploading injection ingestion json jsonl ndjson text stacktrace errors warnings patterns natural uploaded analyse analyze analysis
body: Open Logs, choose a UTF-8 .log, .txt, .jsonl, or .ndjson file up to 2 MB, then Analyze logs. A monitoring connection is not required. Optionally add an incident start and a fallback service name. Findings group recognized errors/warnings with supporting line numbers and excerpts, service counts, timestamp coverage, and optional before/after counts. Download the JSON report to keep it. CoRCA does not persist uploads or reports on the server. These are bounded log observations, not a causal diagnosis, an AI log interpretation, or a continuous log-ingestion pipeline. Missing timestamps limit time comparisons.
summary: Open Logs, choose a UTF-8 .log, .txt, .jsonl, or .ndjson file up to 2 MB, then Analyze logs. Add an incident start if you want before/after counts. Findings show recurring errors and supporting lines, not causal diagnoses. Download the report to keep it; uploads and reports are not stored on the server.

title: Accounts and permissions
keywords: account accounts user users login sign sign-in password passwords administrator admin responder role roles permission permissions access session sso mfa identity audit team activity add person people invite invitation
body: Open Settings → Team & access. A deployment operator creates the first administrator with the local backend.access bootstrap-admin command shown there; there is no default password or public registration. After bootstrap everyone signs in. Administrators create people, manage roles, disable accounts, reset passwords, change monitoring/services/sensitivity/calibration, and review activity. Responders investigate incidents, analyze logs, verify metrics, discover services, and read shared history. Everyone can change their own password with the current password. Password changes/resets, role changes, and disabling an account revoke its sessions. Browser sessions expire after eight hours. Local accounts do not include SSO, MFA, or tenant isolation. Successful configuration changes and audit entries commit together. Without accounts, local access is shared and cannot be attributed to individuals.
summary: Open Settings → Team & access. Administrators add people, manage roles, reset passwords, and review activity. Responders investigate and read shared history. Everyone can change their own password. The first administrator must be created on the deployment host; there is no default password.

title: Backups and recovery
keywords: backup backups restore recovery restart rollback storage database lost history session
body: Workspace settings, diagnoses, alerts, users, and activity persist in SQLite on the deployment volume. Use backend.admin backup for a consistent database snapshot and restore into a new path while the service is stopped. Provider credentials are stored separately and need their matching private files or a fresh connection after restore. The restore CLI removes restored browser sessions. Reconcile account changes against the backup date before reopening access. Set CORCA_REQUIRE_ACCOUNTS=1 after first-administrator bootstrap to refuse account-free startup after an old/empty restore. Interrupted running jobs are requeued on startup. Run one replica; backup/recovery drills and target-environment acceptance are still required. There is no automatic history retention.
summary: Workspace history and settings persist in SQLite. Back up the database and saved provider credentials separately. Restore into a new path while the service is stopped, then verify account access and connections. The restore command revokes restored sessions. Ask your deployment administrator to perform recovery.

title: What is available today
keywords: jenkins patch nightly pipeline ci cd remediation auto fix automate oauth sso mfa tenant enterprise production reliable reliability availability supported limitations limits
body: CoRCA is a self-hosted beta with metrics adapters, investigations, an Alertmanager inbox, uploaded log analysis, local accounts/roles, and configuration activity. Jenkins build/patch-analysis/nightly-review integration is proposed and is not implemented. Automatic remediation, provider OAuth, SSO, MFA, tenant isolation, and multi-replica availability are not implemented. Test counts and fixture success do not establish customer accuracy or production availability. Verify real provider access, alert delivery, independent incident usefulness, load, recovery, and operational ownership for each deployment.
summary: Jenkins integration is not implemented. Automatic remediation, provider OAuth, SSO, MFA, tenant isolation, and multi-replica availability are also unavailable. CoRCA is a self-hosted beta; verify real monitoring, diagnosis usefulness, load, and recovery for your deployment.

title: About this help bot
keywords: help assistant bot chat ai privacy model question questions understand explain guide guides
body: The help bot explains CoRCA using bundled product guides and basic setup status: current screen, role, provider type, service count, and enabled investigation methods. It cannot operate the app, inspect incident evidence, execute commands, or change settings. Without an AI provider, Guide answers find relevant guide excerpts; this is not generative AI. With AI enabled by a deployment administrator, questions and recent chat messages go to OpenAI with the product guides and basic setup status. No logs, raw queries, credentials, service names, alert text, or diagnosis contents are automatically attached. Do not type secrets or sensitive incident data into chat. Chat stays in page memory, is not saved by CoRCA, and clears on reload or Clear chat. AI can be wrong; check the cited guides. Provider-side data policies still apply.
summary: Ask about setup, alerts, results, logs, or team access. Guide answers use local product guides; generative AI is optional and must be configured by an administrator. This bot cannot inspect incident evidence or change settings. Don’t type secrets. Use the source links to check answers.

title: Read evaluation and pipeline results
keywords: eval evals evaluation evaluations quality pipeline pipelines ci nightly benchmark benchmarks score accuracy confidence publish evidence validation
summary: Open Quality to review published evaluations. Diagnosis quality shows confirmed-cause matches, healthy false alarms, sample counts, and unavailable results. Open the scope and limitations before comparing runs. A passed software test run is not proof of incident accuracy. If nothing is published, no score is assumed.
body: Quality displays immutable evaluation summaries published by administrators or a separately scoped pipeline token. The customer view focuses on diagnosis accuracy, confirmed causes, and anomaly detection. Each run shows evidence type, sample counts per metric, date, scope/limitations, publisher, build revision when supplied, and a pipeline link when supplied. Diagnosis pilot assessments can be summarized using backend.quality pilot. Software test reports remain available through CI and the publishing API, outside the customer diagnosis view. Pipelines publish prepared summaries using backend.quality publish, or administrators upload prepared JSON. CoRCA does not execute pipelines or fetch/verify their results independently. A passed declared gate is not production approval. No score is invented for missing evaluations or zero samples. Compare only runs with compatible scope, data, method, and frozen criteria. Pipeline links may require separate access. Raw incident identities and failure output are not part of the summary.
